text:
maria g: Pushed a small docs PR for Private/VPC installs — adds a new 'minimal' installer profile intended for strict air-gapped sites. It trims optional telemetry, removes nonessential example images to reduce tarball size, and adds a checksum manifest + verify step. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4592 - PTAL when you have a sec.

jonathan: Nice. Can you add a short migration note for existing installs? People will worry about telemetry removal and token/secret rotation.

maria g: Yep — added a Migration section describing how to flip profiles with the new `--profile minimal` flag and a one-liner to regenerate certs/tokens. Example: `./installer migrate --from default --to minimal --rotate-secrets`.

ashok: Quick note on HSM behavior — if we remove some containers, the systemd unit for the pkcs11 plugin needs a `Restart=on-failure` and a small `ExecStartPost=` probe, otherwise some HSMs need a warmup. Suggest this snippet for the docs under "HSM considerations":

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Redwood PKCS#11 helper
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/redwood-pkcs11-wrapper --config /etc/redwood/pkcs11.conf
ExecStartPost=/bin/sh -c 'sleep 1; /usr/local/bin/redwood-pkcs11-wrapper --probe || exit 1'
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=3

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

ashok: Also include how to detect common PKCS#11 paths (`/usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so`, `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/pkcs11/`) and a short debug command: `pkcs11-tool --list-slots`.

sam: I wrote a compact JS SDK example for customers behind chained proxies (some on-prem infra route outbound via an egress proxy then a corporate proxy). Posting the snippet to include in SDK examples: 

```js
// Node example: chained proxy with http-proxy-agent + https-proxy-agent
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const { HttpsProxyAgent } = require('https-proxy-agent');
const { HttpProxyAgent } = require('http-proxy-agent');

// hop1 -> corporate proxy, hop2 -> egress appliance
const hop2 = new HttpsProxyAgent('http://egress.internal:3128');
const hop1 = new HttpProxyAgent({ keepAlive: true, proxy: 'http://corp-proxy.corp:8080', agent: hop2 });

fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', { agent: hop1, headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer <KEY>' } })
  .then(r => r.json())
  .then(console.log)
  .catch(err => console.error('proxy err', err));
```

sam: This illustrates explicit agent chaining; I also added a short note about MTLS termination at the egress appliance and when to use `tls.connect` client certs.

leah: Small content/link fixes: we need to update the "Secrets rotation" link in the Migration section — it currently points to the internal runbook path that moved. Replace with `/docs/runbooks/secrets-rotation.md` and add a brief checklist for ticketing (customer notify, schedule downtime window, post-rotation smoke test).

maria g: Good catch, fixed the link and added the checklist bullets (notify -> snapshot -> rotate -> smoke).

jonathan: One more ask — can we include an offline verification step for the checksum manifest so operators can run it without internet? Something like `sha256sum -c manifest.sha256` plus instructions for packing the `manifest.sha256` into the airgap tarball.

maria g: Added the exact command and example manifest format:

```
# manifest.sha256
sha256sum 12345abcd...  redwood-installer.tar.gz
sha256sum ffeedd00...  payload-images.tar.gz
```

and the verify step: `sha256sum -c manifest.sha256`.

sam: LGTM for SDK snippet, I tweaked wording to call out Node 16+ compatibility.
